service.name: Corporate retreat entertainment in Breckenridge
service.serviceType: Live music for corporate retreats and incentive events
service.description: Live music for corporate retreats and private celebrations at Breckenridge venues, solo through quartet, planned for 9,600 feet at published resort rates.

faqs.q: Does 9,600 feet change what the band costs?
faqs.a: The price reads from the same published resort column as the other corridor towns, plus the flat $600 travel line. What changes at Breckenridge is the plan: the generous end of the load-in window, a longer sound check, paced sets and retunes between them. There is no altitude line on the quote.

Reported at 55 dBA by day and 50 after hours in residential zones, 70 and 65 in commercial, with the town manager able to permit above them. We could not reach the code text directly, so we treat your venue's number as governing and build the night under it. Sources are cited on our mountain corridor page.

faqs.q: How does load-in work at Ten Mile Station?
faqs.a: Over snow in winter, on the venue's own access and schedule, and by vehicle in the warm months. We settle what travels, when it travels and where cases wait with the venue in writing before the day, and we take the generous end of the published 45 to 90 minute load-in window.

faqs.q: How late can the music run?
faqs.a: To the curfew as written, and we want the time at booking rather than on the night. The last twenty minutes are shaped to land on it, and time added before the cut-off bills at the same hourly figure as every earlier hour, in 30-minute increments. There is no overtime rate.

faqs.q: Do peak ski weekends cost more?
faqs.a: Holiday and peak weekends carry +25% and New Year's Eve +50%, both published on the rate card rather than quoted late. The base figure still reads from the resort column, and travel stays the same flat $600 line whatever the date.
